text: With the actual board components underneath and the board fully seated, the locating posts must project far enough for the retaining clips to engage.
Use a flat thumb contact area on the centre mouse paddle so the same thumb can touch it and click the mouse switch.

Make the part of each locating post that passes through the DFR0030 V2 mounting hole thicker so the board cannot rock. Keep the narrower neck at the top for the easy flat clips and preserve the successful post height. Allow for hole pitch, board tolerance and printed PETG fit so the board seats without damaging it.

The DFRobot DFR0030 manufacturer product page specifies two nominal 3 mm mounting holes. No finished-hole tolerance is stated. R69 retains the earlier shaped locating posts, nominally 2.25 by 2.52 mm; the user reports board play in the fitted print. These posts are separate from the hinge pin and bore.

Revise the retaining clips together with the touch-board posts so the fitted board is held snugly without wobble, while remaining removable and avoiding PCB stress. Retain the current successful post height.

The fitted R70 touch board still wobbles around its locating posts and clips. The post height is satisfactory. The exact real finished-hole diameter, tolerance and contribution of clip play have not been measured.
Use the earlier flat slide-on clips for the DFRobot posts. Both clips should install easily and retain the touch board, preserving the successful post height.
When fitting the R78 touch-board clips, the user reported that one piece tore off because installation required too much force. The exact torn feature was not identified.
On the fitted R79 assembly the touch board still wobbled on the posts with the flat clips. The actual hole diameter and amount and direction of play have not been measured.
